title: Anda: Unlocking Efficient LLM Inference with a Variable-Length Grouped Activation Data Format
problem: Weight-only quantized LLMs retain floating-point (FP) activations for accuracy, which shifts the energy and latency bottleneck to costly FP memory accesses and FP-INT GEMM computation; existing LLM accelerators optimize computation alone without jointly addressing data representation and movement for FP activations.
motivation: FP-INT GEMM dominates LLM inference cost, and the FP activation format is simultaneously memory-bandwidth-hungry and compute-inefficient; a co-designed adaptive format can cut both footprints without sacrificing accuracy.
method: Anda proposes a new adaptive activation data type with a group-shared exponent and dynamically allocated mantissa bits per group, enabling variable precision per LLM module. An iterative post-training precision search algorithm determines per-module bit-widths to balance accuracy and efficiency without retraining. On the hardware side, Anda uses a bit-plane-based data organization, bit-serial computation processing elements, and a runtime bit-plane compressor to simultaneously shrink storage, computation, and memory footprint. The result is a hardware-software co-designed accelerator targeting FP-INT GEMM in LLMs.
key_novelty: The Anda data type: a variable-length grouped format with shared exponent and dynamic mantissa allocation that adapts precision per LLM module, jointly optimizing FP data movement and computation for FP-INT GEMM.
contributions: Anda adaptive data format with group-shared exponent and dynamic mantissa bit allocation for variable-precision FP activations.
Iterative post-training precision search algorithm for per-module bit-width optimization without retraining.
Hardware suite: bit-plane data organization, bit-serial Anda-enhanced processing units, and runtime bit-plane compressor.
2.4x speedup, 4.0x area efficiency, and 3.1x energy efficiency improvement over GPU-like FP-FP baseline on OPT, LLaMA, LLaMA-2.
baselines: GPU-like FP-FP baseline for FP-INT GEMM
limitations: Evaluated only on FP-INT GEMM operations (weight-only quantization setting); does not address fully quantized (INT-INT) or purely FP inference scenarios.
primary_theme: Adaptive variable-precision activation data format and accelerator for efficient FP-INT LLM GEMM
